student.question: Do students need their own API key or chat account?
student.answer: No. Signing in with the organization account gives access to the platform's unified model capability.

student.question: Do the computer lab and classroom PCs work?
student.answer: Yes — the public client supports macOS (Apple silicon) and 64-bit Windows.

student.question: Can we run Arduino and micro:bit lessons?
student.answer: Yes — classroom practice with Arduino Uno and micro:bit is supported.

student.question: What happens when an organization runs out of credits?
student.answer: The organization console prompts teachers to top up; once topped up, students can continue. The platform never blocks students over compute usage.

teacher.question: What should teachers prepare before class?
teacher.answer: Students sign in with the organization account and open the class in a browser — lab PCs need nothing installed.

teacher.question: Where can teachers see student work and usage?
teacher.answer: The organization console shows usage records and works, and can publish outstanding works to the gallery.

org.question: Do students need their own API key?
org.answer: No. The organization creates student accounts, and API access plus compute are already built in — students just start class.

org.question: What courses does the platform provide?
org.answer: Lingdong Courses offers standard course packs (with slides and lesson plans); organizations can schedule them directly.

org.question: What is the curriculum, and what ages is it for?
org.answer: The curriculum is designed for ages 8–16, with 48 lessons in total: Stage 1 — AI Magic Starter Camp (16 lessons), Stage 2 — AI Humanities & Digital Exploration Camp (16 lessons), Stage 3 — AI Full-stack Application Camp (16 lessons).

org.question: How are classes run? Can our own teachers teach them?
org.answer: We use a “standardized system + teacher guidance” model: existing coding teachers can teach after training. The system includes complete courseware, step-by-step guidance, AI tools, an asset library and work management, so teachers do not need to build slides, find tools or write code — they follow the lesson plan and answer questions.

org.question: Is the system safe? Could children see inappropriate content?
org.answer: It is a closed, teaching-only environment. All content, tools and assets are reviewed by our curriculum team; there is no access to external websites, no ads and no inappropriate content, fully meeting youth online-safety standards.

org.question: AI changes so fast — will the courses go out of date?
org.answer: That is exactly the strength of this model. Our curriculum team tracks the frontier and updates lessons, tools and courseware as AI products and models evolve — partner organizations get every update for free.

about.body: National and local education authorities keep pushing AI education in K-12: courses must be offered in full, and generative AI must be usable and governable. What organizations really need is a complete solution — one that fits the timetable, keeps accounts and usage under control, and produces a work in every lesson.

series_ee83eed5780a46489d2c.title: S1: AI Magic Starter Camp
series_ee83eed5780a46489d2c.description: An entry-level AI course for ages 8–16 with no prior experience. Starting from playful interaction, students get to know AI tools and basic prompting, then create AI artwork, stories, simple animations and block-based coding projects — building early AI literacy along with expression, imagination and logical thinking.

series_5b64dc87d89a43419ee8.title: S2: AI Humanities & Digital Explorer Camp
series_5b64dc87d89a43419ee8.description: A cross-disciplinary course for ages 9–16 who already have some AI basics. It breaks the boundary between tools and subjects, applying AI to Chinese, history, English and maths through hands-on tasks such as old-photo restoration, classical-poetry illustration, an English conversation assistant and a personal bookkeeping tool. Students learn to turn knowledge into visible work.

series_d18516029446496fac5f.title: S3: AI Full-Stack Project Camp
series_d18516029446496fac5f.description: An advanced project course for ages 10–16 with AI and coding basics. Centred on complete projects — PPT automation, information-organising tools, a private knowledge base, a smart customer-service system and age-friendly apps — students go from requirements to a finished product, building systems thinking, project skills and engineering habits. Outcomes can be used for science fairs and portfolio reviews.
